Commentary.Commentary: So, that is it from this game. Bangladesh taken on India in the finals on 9th February 2020. On the other end, New Zealand take Pakistan on for the 3rd place playoffs. On 7th February 2020, Australia take on West Indies for the 5th place playoffs. That game begins at 1000 local ( 0800 GMT). Till then take care and cheers!

Bangladesh skipper, Akbar Ali says the bowlers did a very good job in restricting them and the batters built partnership which was necessary. Says the spinners were bowling well and they had a plan against New Zealand. On Hasan Joy, Ali says he is exceptional and the hard work they put in the nets has paid off. Further adds that it is a treat to watch him bat. On playing their first ever Under-19 Finals, Akbar say that they will play the Finals as a normal game and not take any pressure. Adds India is a top side and they need to bring their A game. Tell Bangladesh fans are passionate and he hopes that they keep supporting them.

New Zealand skipper, Jesse Tashkoff admits it was a tough toss to lose and credits the Bangladesh bowlers for the way they played. Adds there was moisture earlier on and the sun later in the day made it easy to bat. Tells it was tough to adjust to batting first for the first time in the tournament but adds they did well to get in the position after the situation they found themselves in. Praises Beckham Wheeler-Greenall for the innings he played and for the attitude he showed. Adds he is proud of his boys and says they are now looking to win the game against Pakistan and finish the tournament on a high. Ends by thanking the fans for their support throughout the tournament.

For his match winning century, Mahmudul Hasan Joy is named the Man of the Match. Hasan Joy says he was just looking to rotate the strike as his role is to bat till the end. Says last time he missed on a century against New Zealand but this time he was not going to miss that. Tells he is feeling very good and thanks the Almighty.

Earlier in the day after losing the toss, New Zealand struggled to get going and it looked like they would not be able to get to 180 but Beckham Wheeler-Greenall's unbeaten 75 took them to a decent total of 211. Shoriful Islam and Hasan Murad were the tormentor-in-chief as they picked up 5 wickets amongst themselves with the former picking up 3.

A tough day, a day of despair for the Kiwis. Once again it is the semi-finals stage that they have faltered. It was a tough day with the ball for the Kiwis. They needed wickets at regular intervals but apart from the start they could not manage to do it in the middle. They came up against a young sensation who was just not going to back down and the Kiwis had no answer to that Bangla Tiger. The bowlers though bowled their hearts out but the runs on the board were not enough for them to defend. 4 off the 6 bowlers used got into the wickets column but all of them had just one each and that was not good enough on the day. New Zealand won't play India in the finals but they will meet their neighbors Pakistan for the 3rd Place Playoff game.

Chasing 212, Bangladesh got off to a poor start losing 2 early wickets. After that what we saw was just brilliance. Mahmudul Hasan Joy first steadied the ship with Towhid Hridoy. The duo added 68 before Hridoy departed. Hasan Joy then took control of the game and showed all of us a masterclass in batting. He played the role of aggressor and stitched a 101-run stand with Shahadat Hossain, getting to his century in the process. He was not able to finish the game for his side but he dragged them inches towards the finish line. The skipper and Hossain sprayed the sprinkles on top of the cake as the Bangla Tigers roared into the Under-19 World Cup Finals.

Bangladesh have done it. The Bangladesh players are running in joy and the reason for that is Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Remember the name. He has single-handedly played a supreme knock under pressure and has taken his country to its first ever World Cup final. It is going to be an all Asian affair in the finals on Sunday here at Senwes Park, Potchefstroom.

WIDE! Short ball outside off, Joy ducks under it. The umpire gives it a wide.
Length ball outside off, Joy plays it to point.
Good length and on off, blocked off the back foot towards covers.
Length ball outside off, Joy leaves it for the keeper.
Length ball outside off, Joy plays it to point and takes a run.
Full ball outside off, Joy drives it straight to covers.
Full ball on leg, Joy looks to flick it but misses it. The ball takes the pads on its way to the keeper. The keeper there appeals for a catch but the umpire is unmoved.
Length ball outside off, Joy pushes the ball to mid off off the back foot.
Mahmudul Hasan Joy is the next batsman in.

OUT! Caught! First blow for New Zealand. The Kiwis have finally broken the stand that was starting to flourish.  Full and wide outside off, Tanzid Hasan cannot resist the temptation to go for it. He goes chasing after it like a kid chasing candy. He looks to cut but it goes off the outside edge towards third man. David Hancock comes in and takes a simple catch. New Zealand needed an early wicket and they have got one but they do not have any time to rest as they need to keep doing this.
Short and on middle, Hasan pulls it but straight to mid-wicket.
Length ball on middle, blocked off the back foot.
FOUR! He has been doing it and this time he connects. Short ball on middle and leg, Emon pulls it with disdain through mid-wicket and fetches the boundary.
On a length and on off, Emon keeps it out off the back foot.
Short ball on middle, Emon looks to hook it but takes his eyes off in the process. The ball bounces a bit more over him and goes to the keeper.
Back of a length ball on off, Emon blocks it off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, Emon is beaten once again. He fails to lay wood on the ball as he looks to defend it.
FOUR LEG BYES! Clarke sprays one down the leg side and Hasan looks to flick it. He misses it. The ball goes to the fine leg fence off his thigh pads. The umpire gives it as leg byes.
Short of a length ball on off, Hasan presents the full face of the bat and blocks it to the off side off the back foot.
BEATEN! Length ball outside off, Hasan looks to block it but the ball goes past the outside edge and into the mitts of the keeper.
Short of a length ball outside off, Emon cuts it through point and takes a single.
On a good length and outside off, Hasan taps it to point and takes a quick single.
Length ball outside off, Hasan looks to squeeze it to the off side but is late to do so. The ball also keeps low as it goes to the keeper past the outside edge.
Another length ball on off, Emon does well to defend it off the back foot.
Good length and around off, blocked off the back foot to covers.
WIDE! Length ball but down the leg side. Emon chooses not to play. The umpire gives it a wide.
FOUR! Overpitched and punished! Full ball outside off, Emon just leans and drives the ball through covers. The ball runs to the fence in a flash. First boundary of the chase.
Still there is  bounce on this track. Emon looks to defend the ball outside his off stump but the ball bounces a bit extra and goes past the outside edge.
Length delivery outside off, Emon shoulders arms to it.
Short of a length ball outside off, Emon looks to pull it but fails to do so as the ball sails over to the keeper.
Length ball around off, Emon pushes the ball through covers and retains the strike.
On a good length and outside off, Emon does not fiddle with it.
Good length ball outside off, Emon looks to defend it off the back foot but the ball sneaks past the outside edge and the ball rises high as the keeper collects it near his face.
Length ball outside off, left alone by Emon this time.
WIDE! Length ball outside off, near the tramline this time. A wide called by the umpire.
Length ball outside off, Emon squeezes the drive between cover and point. Both the fielders run behind the ball and field it. The batsmen get a couple.
Length ball on middle and leg, Hasan flicks it towards mid-wicket and takes a run.
Kristian Clarke to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Length ball around off, Emon blocks it to covers off the back foot. End of a very good over from Joey Field.
WIDE! Length ball outside off, Emon does not play as it is too wide. The umpire calls it a wide.
Length ball on leg, Hasan flicks it to mid-wicket and gets off the mark with a single.
Length ball on middle and leg, Emon flicks it towards square leg and Bangladesh are off the mark.
Three leaves in a row. Another ball outside off and Emon does not bother to play at it.
Another ball that is angled across the left-hander and Emon lets it through to the keeper.
Field starts with a length ball outside off and Emon lets it be.

We are back for the chase. The two Bangladesh openers Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan will open the batting. New Zealand players are in a huddle and they disperse now on the field. Joey Field will start the proceedings for New Zealand.
